sentences.text:
According to the prosecution case, Food Inspector Satish Kumar Dhakad visited the shop of petitioner known as firm Manoj Brothers, Gast ka Taziya, Lashkar, Gwalior and due to suspicion, samples of Rajdarbar Gutkha, Sanjog Gutkha,
Shankar Gutkha and Vimal Gutkha were taken and sent to laboratory test to State Laboratory,
Bhopal.

It is alleged that on 13.6.2011, report of Public Analyst was received and it was found that the samples are mis-branded/adulterated and thereafter the sanction was obtained from the Deputy Director of Local Health Authority and the private complaint was filed before the trial Court.

During the course of trial, petitioner filed an application under Section 20 (A) of the Act for arraying the distributor Agrawal Agency as an accused in the case but the application (Annexure P-4) was dismissed by the trial Court vide order dated 10.9.2022.

Against the order passed by the trial Court,
criminal revision was filed before the Sessions Court which was also dismissed by the order impugned.
Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the orders passed by the Courts below are neither legal nor just and hence, liable to be set aside.
He has further argued that admittedly the petitioner is not the manufacturer of gutkha and, therefore, the dismissal of application is against the settled principle of law and provisions of the Act.

Since the petitioner is facing charge of misbranding,
therefore, the distributor Agrawal Agency, who supplied the gutkha, ought to be arrayed as an accused in the case otherwise defence of the petitioner would be prejudiced and he will be deprived to get justice in the case, therefore, the petition be allowed, impugned orders be set aside and the distributor Agrawal Agency be arrayed as accused in the case.

In support of his submissions, learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon the judgment passed by the ALOK KUMAR 2022.11.23 12:25:39 +05'30' 11.0.23 Supreme Court in the case of Alkem Laboratories Ltd. (M/s.) v. State of M.P. & Another, [Criminal Case No. 1798 of 2019; arising from SLP (Cr.) No. 3995 of 2018 decided on 29.11.2019].

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned State counsel supported the impugned orders and prayed for rejection of the petition.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the available record.

Section 20 (A) of the Act reads as below:
"Power of court to implead manufacturer, etc.- Where at any time during the trial of any offence under this Act alleged to have been committed by any person, not being the manufacturer, distributor or dealer of any article of food, the court is satisfied, on the evidence adduced before it, that such manufacturer, distributor or dealer is also concerned with that offence, then, the court may, notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (3) of section 319 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), or in section 20 proceed against him as though a prosecution had been instituted against him under section 20."

sentences.text: The provision of Section 20 (A) of the Act as mentioned above specifically provides that the satisfaction of Court is necessary for arraying the manufacturer as an accused and for satisfaction of the Court there must be evidence that such manufacturer/distributor/dealer is concerned with the offence.

The perusal of Annexure P-3 (bills of purchase of as many as eight articles) does not indicate that it is the bill of the same articles whose samples were taken by the Food Inspector, therefore, the impugned orders passed by ALOK KUMAR 2022.11.23 12:25:50 +05'30' 11.0.23 the Courts below rejecting the application under Section 20 (A) of the Act of the petitioner as well as the revision does not found to be against the facts available on record.
In the opinion of this Court, there is no illegality or jurisdictional error in the orders impugned warranting interference while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 of CrPC.
Consequently, present petition sans merit and is hereby dismissed.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE AKS ALOK KUMAR 2022.11.23 12:26:00 +05'30' 11.0.23 Manoj Vijjan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 22 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19366744/
